title: Map existing hierarchical planning and guarded execution boundaries
request: Read the complete planning package and inspect the current DCLab repository. Complete TP-01A architecture and capability mapping only, without runtime or contract implementation or proceeding to TP-01B.
spec: engineering/planning/TP_01A.txt; the current repository is authoritative. Deliver three guides, exact mandatory workflow and registry inventories, ownership and recovery decisions, a Telco binary design slice, acceptance gates and a verified handoff.
plan: Read the README, master and every implementation prompt in order; inspect the current checkout and preserve unrelated work.
Trace planning contracts, engine and programme calls, registry guards, human gates, storage, checkpoints and evidence readback.
Produce a static source audit and readable guides; distinguish conceptual checks from physical stage actions.
Cross-check the inventory against runtime metadata without invoking handlers, run focused regressions and the package gate, and obtain adversarial review.
Record actual outcomes, update only the TP-01A tracker and stop with a TP-01B contract handoff.

decisions.decision: Keep TP-01A documentation and source investigation only.
decisions.why: Its specific instructions forbid runtime and public contract changes. A missing-document precheck and metadata coverage checks are appropriate; a toy runtime implementation would exceed scope.

decisions.decision: Reuse SolutionTeam, Registry, studio graph and engine, atomic Programme, existing stores and checkpoints.
decisions.why: They already own dispatch, human gates, science and persistence. Task planning must add evidence-backed structure without a parallel engine or database.

decisions.decision: Separate immutable structural graph revisions from mutable execution attempts and receipts.
decisions.why: Checkpoint state and descriptive workflow steps do not prove a side effect completed. Recovery must compare current inputs with durable owner evidence.

decisions.decision: Treat shared conceptual steps as checks attached to one stage action.
decisions.why: Data prepares the split and summaries, models chooses on validation, and final includes threshold and the protected score. Separate actions for each concept could duplicate fits or holdout reads.

decisions.decision: Require current approved source admission and block unknown final outcomes on the future opt-in path.
decisions.why: Legacy optional approval flags and saved counters do not provide complete revision binding or a durable receipt after every crash boundary. Contracts may describe these blockers but cannot claim safe automatic retry.

change: Added architecture, capability matrix and acceptance guides, an expanded static source audit, corrected the planning README paths and prepared a TP-01A progress handoff. No existing runtime or public contract was modified.

findings.defect: The planning README pointed to a missing codex directory and a master filename that did not match the supplied files.
findings.scenario: A later session follows the documented path and cannot open the next package even though its prompt is present in the flat directory.
findings.cause: The delivered directory shape differed from the README example.
findings.fix: Updated README links and directory shape to the actual flat inputs instead of creating duplicate prompts.
findings.test: Documentation link and source existence checks pass after correcting the source references.

findings.defect: A mandatory workflow human gate is stronger than the unchanged legacy runtime defaults and legacy approvals lack complete current input binding.
findings.scenario: A future task runner treats a valid workflow or an unused older approval as current permission to execute final scoring.
findings.cause: Workflow validation, solution signature and execution permission are separate existing mechanisms.
findings.fix: Documented explicit approved-source admission and current revision binding as requirements before future dispatch; preserved legacy behavior.
findings.test: Existing graph regression tests and source review establish current behavior; new admission tests belong to the later dispatch package.
findings.open: Later dispatch must implement revision-bound admission through the existing approval owner.

findings.defect: A crash after final scoring but before durable counter and evidence persistence can leave an ambiguous read outcome in unchanged execution code.
findings.scenario: A future resume path sees a failed stage and a zero saved count, retries final, and reads the protected holdout again.
findings.cause: Checkpoint, scientific effect and project counter writes are not one durable transaction or receipt protocol.
findings.fix: Recorded a mandatory unknown-outcome blocker and owner-level intent, receipt and reconciliation requirements for execution and recovery packages.
findings.test: Source inspection of engine and programme write ordering; no deliberate holdout crash run was performed in this design-only package.
findings.open: Automatic final retry must remain blocked until the original execution owners expose sufficient durable proof.

findings.defect: Normal tabular split evidence records source, settings and seed but does not persist a dedicated membership digest for every kind.
findings.scenario: A verifier claims immutable split membership from a descriptive lock step even though only reproducibility metadata is stored.
findings.cause: Workflow acceptance wording is stricter than the evidence available on some existing paths.
findings.fix: Documented evidence-specific limits and required blockers instead of asserting a guarantee or adding a second split action.
findings.test: Mandatory step inventory cross-checks actual producer fields and source references.
findings.open: Later verification must obtain adequate split proof through its owner or block the strict criterion.

measurements.name: Initial documentation acceptance
measurements.gate: All three required TP-01A guide files must exist before acceptance.
measurements.result: All three required guides were absent before this package.
measurements.next: Create the guides and verify complete source-linked coverage.

measurements.name: Existing planning and guard regressions
measurements.gate: The seven selected contract, workflow, mapping, graph and runtime test files must pass without live model calls.
measurements.result: 256 tests passed across seven files with no skips in 26.0 seconds.
limits: Existing tests do not measure a task planner that has not been implemented.

measurements.name: Source-linked architecture coverage
measurements.gate: Every mandatory family-step pair and registered tool must match live metadata and every audited source hash must still match, without invoking any tool handler.
measurements.result: 105 mandatory pairs, 28 step IDs, 18 audit columns, 105 tools and 105 contracts matched; 54 audited source hashes and document links passed.
limits: This checks the mapping against this checkout, not future execution effectiveness.

measurements.name: Adversarial architecture review
measurements.gate: The repository reviewer must find no unresolved correctness issue in the TP-01A mapping and authority boundaries.
measurements.result: Reviewer independently matched the step, tool, source and contract inventories and returned PASS with no correctness findings.
limits: Future runtime fixes and execution receipts have not been implemented.

measurements.name: Existing adapter and execution-boundary regressions
measurements.gate: All selected adapter, workflow readback, programme and SolutionTeam tests must pass offline without skips.
measurements.result: 104 tests passed across four files and 72 execution units in 274.5 seconds with no skips. The first sandbox attempt was blocked before execution by the local multiprocessing socket; the identical approved local run passed.
limits: Fixture runs do not establish safe crash recovery for the new task layer.

measurements.name: Repository package gate
measurements.gate: make check-quick must pass applicable tests on file storage and PostgreSQL plus all freshness and evidence gates.
measurements.result: 23 tests on file storage and 10 tests on PostgreSQL passed without skips; all 10 rd-gates passed. Product flows were not reached by this documentation-only change.
limits: Full rd-check, core wheel rebuild and comparative or sealed benchmarks were not run for this design-only package.

outcome: TP-01A complete: source coverage, 360 focused regression tests, the repository package gate and adversarial review passed. Only documentation, static audit and development trajectory/generated corpus changed. TP-01B remains unstarted and is ready for pure additive contract work; automatic execution remains blocked by the documented future receipt and approval requirements. A single reviewable commit is proposed; no commit or push was performed.
lessons: Trace actual execution boundaries before translating descriptive workflow steps into actions.
A registry read label does not establish a pure planning operation.
Distinguish workflow validity, human approval, completed evidence and a safely retryable effect.
risks: Repeated side effects if conceptual steps are mapped one-to-one to existing stage calls.
False completion from stale evidence or mutable checkpoint status.
Scope expansion into runtime work before the design package is accepted.
